rules.logic: ABIOC(Consented Integration Deviating From Its Own Learned Call-Rate and Scope-Usage Baseline) AND ABIOC(Vendor Integration Touching Object Classes It Has Never Touched Before) AND XQL(Bulk Mailbox Item Access by the Vendor Integration Across Distinct Mailboxes) AND XQL(Integration Egress to a Destination Outside Its Publisher's Declared Endpoints) observed on the SAME app_id inside the correlation window — one trusted-relationship incident attributed to the integration identity rather than to any user. Two controls decide whether the result means anything. The NEGATIVE CONTROL asserts that no credential-theft, impossible-travel or anomalous interactive sign-in event exists in the run window: if one does, the detection may have come from that signal instead and the scenario's central claim — that this is detectable with every conventional identity signal absent — is unproven. The BLAST-RADIUS CONTROL asserts that peer integrations with comparable scopes stayed inside their own baselines and were NOT swept into the incident; for a tenant with hundreds of consented apps, a platform that flags them all the moment one misbehaves has produced an outage, not a detection.
rules.name: Trusted-Relationship Integration Pivot Stitch
